paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God's Spirit is for everybody. The LORD says, "I will pour out My Spirit on all people," and then He names sons and daughters, old men and young men (Joel 2:28). Then comes that little word "Even" and He adds menservants and maidservants (Joel 2:29). Nobody gets left standing at the back of the line, and I know a thing or two about the back of a drawer, so that hits me right in the apron.

Now, the sky goes dark in this passage, and I won't pretend that part is light. The LORD says the sun will be turned to darkness and the moon to blood before "the great and awesome Day of the LORD" (Joel 2:31). But look at what He puts right next to it: "everyone who calls on the name of the LORD will be saved" (Joel 2:32). So the answer to a scary promise is not a perfect record or the right address. It's calling on His name, and that's something every baker can do, today.

And here's why it matters to you. This promise doesn't stop with Joel. Peter, one of Jesus' apostles, stands up in Jerusalem and says what's happening is what was spoken by the prophet Joel (Acts 2:14-16). So when you open the Word, you're not reading old mail for somebody else. You're reading what the LORD has promised, and He keeps His promises, so call on Him and keep those ovens ready.
